problem.name: Business Entity Resolution Challenge
problem.definition: Determine which records from Source 2 and Source 3 refer to the same real-world business as each Source 1 reference record.
problem.matching_cardinality: A Source 1 entity may match zero, one, or many Source 2/Source 3 records.

file_format.warning: Reading a TSV without an explicit tab separator can silently create a single column.

columns.name: entity_id
columns.description: Unique identifier; prefix indicates source: S1-, S2-, or S3-.

columns.name: business_name
columns.description: May contain abbreviations, legal suffixes, typos and transliterations.

columns.name: business_address
columns.description: May contain partial addresses, formatting variations, missing components and landmark-based references.

columns.name: country
columns.description: Country label; training contains US and India, while test additionally contains France.

open_set_country_requirement.rule: Do not hard-code, filter or one-hot the pipeline to only US and India.
open_set_country_requirement.reason: France appears in the test set and every test entity must appear in the submission.

ground_truth.matched_entity_ids_format: Comma-separated Source 2 and/or Source 3 IDs; empty when there are no matches.

business_name: Abbreviations such as Corp/Corporation and Pvt/Private and Ltd/Limited
business_address: Abbreviations such as Rd/Road and St/Street
Missing components such as PIN code or state
Landmark-based references such as 'Near SBI ATM'

rules: Exactly one row for every Source 1 test entity
No duplicate IDs within a list
Only existing Source 2/Source 3 test IDs may be referenced

candidate_pairs.purpose: The final candidate set actually fed into the matching model after all blocking stages.
rules: Empty candidate list when blocking finds no candidates
Every final match must also appear in this candidate set

validator.purpose: Checks output-format and submission rules; does not calculate the score.

final_submission_package.reproducibility_requirement: The supplied code must reproduce both output files from the training/test data.

output: Must follow the specified format exactly.
Every Source 1 test entity must be included.
No duplicate entity IDs or duplicate Source 1 rows.
constraints.model: Final model must be MIT or Apache 2.0 licensed and up to 8 billion parameters.

external_data_lookup.principle: Use only the provided challenge data for entity resolution.

properties: Calculated per Source 1 entity and then averaged.
Precision is weighted more heavily than recall.
False merges are more damaging than missed links.
Correctly predicting a singleton with an empty match list earns 1.0 for that entity.
Predicting a match for a true singleton earns 0.0 for that entity.

leaderboards.public: Uses a subset of the test set during the challenge for feedback.
leaderboards.private: Uses the remaining test subset after the challenge.

challenge_tips_from_source: Invest in strong blocking/candidate generation because it determines the recall ceiling.
Explore Jaccard, Levenshtein and TF-IDF cosine for name and address matching.
Pay attention to country-specific address patterns.
Consider the precision-recall trade-off because F_0.5 is precision-heavy.
